title: [CQ-M01b] Versioned policy snapshot identity
description:
Objective: Extend the landed CQ-M01a pure primitives with sufficient configuration provenance for durable task/attempt snapshots, without introducing another revision or approval authority.

Deliverable: Define a strict v2 configuration snapshot with version, profile, canonical planRevision and captured deliveryPolicy, plus optional Task/ExecutionAttempt snapshot fields. Keep the existing v1 decoder compatible but never infer a missing strict deliveryPolicy from current settings or treat v1 as certified authorization. Reuse resolveDeliveryPolicy/DELIVERY_POLICIES; if rehomed, preserve policy.ts exports and its absent/null compatibility, avoiding a circular import or a second enum/decoder authority. Preserve live deliveryPolicy behavior for absent/legacy/observe workflows. Required-check definition/destination provenance remains later contract/check/delivery work, not an implicit claim made by v2.

Existing implementation surfaces / proposed focused tests (maximum five files): packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts; packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionProfile.ts; packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionProfile.test.ts; packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/policy.ts; proposed new packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionPolicySnapshot.test.ts.

NOT in scope: Task/attempt persistence, lifecycle wiring, trusted approval identity, F03/F04/F05 behavior, check-definition certification, runner activation, and old held-out delivery-test edits. Verification (fresh, exit 0): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test -- --maxWorkers=4. Run in a synchronized isolated copy with native Linux dependencies and Linux-only PATH; preserve the original Windows node_modules and unchanged package-lock.json. Each slice owns its behavior tests, one final verification/adversarial review, and no production activation. This breakdown defines deliverables, not per-task implementation steps.
definitionOfDone: Focused tests accept exact valid v2 values and preserve captured deliveryPolicy and canonical safe-integer planRevision; malformed/null/unknown/extra fields fail closed.
Existing valid v1 decoding remains compatible, while a v1 strict snapshot cannot manufacture missing policy identity from current project settings.
Snapshot results do not alias caller inputs; tests mutate decoded copies without changing originals.
Existing deliveryPolicy exports and absent/null defaults remain behaviorally identical; absent/legacy/observe profiles do not silently freeze or relax existing live policy.
Pure types/helpers do not imply approval/readiness; verified-local remains unconditionally EXECUTION_PROFILE_NOT_READY and has no environment/caller bypass.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test -- --maxWorkers=4` exits 0 in the synchronized native-Linux copy, with actual pass/skip counts and output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: Do not enable verified-local or claim approval, runner trust, hardware/isolation certification, or verified completion from a configuration snapshot.
Do not edit packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts or weaken existing held-out delivery assertions; add focused tests for new behavior.
No direct .moe edits or Git writes; wrappers own landing. Keep each implementation plan within five source/test files and normal sizing limits.

implementationPlan.description: Types + leaf decoder. (a) packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts is CRLF in this checkout: edit in place and keep CRLF. Replace the v1-only ExecutionPolicySnapshot with `ExecutionPolicySnapshotV1 { version: 1; profile: ExecutionProfile; planRevision: number }`, `ExecutionPolicySnapshotV2 { version: 2; profile: ExecutionProfile; planRevision: number; deliveryPolicy: DeliveryPolicy }` and `export type ExecutionPolicySnapshot = ExecutionPolicySnapshotV1 | ExecutionPolicySnapshotV2`. Reword the doc: a CONFIGURATION identity captured with the canonical Task.planRevision - NOT plan approval, model receipt, runner trust, isolation readiness, a required-check definition, a delivery destination or verified completion (drop the current 'for an approved revision' wording); v1 carries no deliveryPolicy identity and nothing may fill one in from current settings. Add `executionPolicySnapshot?: ExecutionPolicySnapshot` to Task (right after planRevision) and to ExecutionAttempt (after presenceAt), each documented: absent on every existing record; no daemon path writes or trusts it yet (capture and ownership guards are separate rollout work), so decode it with readExecutionPolicySnapshot and never read it as approval or readiness. (b) packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/executionProfile.ts must stay a LEAF: runtime imports only ../util/errors.js, schema imports type-only; it must never import policy.ts or any state store. Move VERBATIM from policy.ts, with their comments: the type-keyed `POLICIES: Record<DeliveryPolicy, true>` record, `export const DELIVERY_POLICIES = Object.keys(POLICIES) as DeliveryPolicy[]` (same order, same unfrozen array - do not freeze) and `export const DEFAULT_DELIVERY_POLICY: DeliveryPolicy = 'legacy'`. Add `export function isDeliveryPolicy(value: unknown): value is DeliveryPolicy` = typeof string + Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(POLICIES, value), exactly the membership test resolveDeliveryPolicy uses today (never DELIVERY_POLICIES.includes). Extend readExecutionPolicySnapshot: keep the undefined -> undefined return and the object/plain-prototype guards; read `version` once and pick the exact own-key set (1 -> version, profile, planRevision with the existing message; 2 -> those plus deliveryPolicy, message naming all four); any other version -> invalidInput('executionPolicySnapshot.version', 'must be 1 or 2'); decode profile with decodeProfile and planRevision with the unchanged non-negative safe-integer rule (same domain as taskStore.decodeStoredPlanRevision, no coercion); for v2 require isDeliveryPolicy(deliveryPolicy) else invalidInput('executionPolicySnapshot.deliveryPolicy', `must be one of: ${DELIVERY_POLICIES.join(', ')}`) - snapshots get NO absent/null -> legacy default. Error handling: every malformed input throws INVALID_INPUT before anything is returned (fail closed, never coerced). Return a fresh literal holding only that version's fields. Add `export function readCapturedDeliveryPolicy(raw: unknown): DeliveryPolicy | undefined` (decode; v2 -> its deliveryPolicy; absent or v1 -> undefined). It deliberately takes no settings; its doc says it is identity only, not the effective policy (absent/legacy/observe tasks keep the live settings.deliveryPolicy). Leave resolveExecutionProfile / resolveTaskExecutionProfile / assertExecutionProfileReady logic unchanged (the union flows through); only reword comments that call a snapshot 'verified' or 'approved'. Define no ordering or ranking between delivery policies (no generic max()).

planningNotes.risks:
- A leaf -> policy.ts import (even type-only is fine, a runtime one is not) silently reintroduces the future attemptStore cycle. Check the import lines.
- Freezing DELIVERY_POLICIES or changing its order, type or message text breaks 'behaviorally identical'. Membership must use POLICIES via isDeliveryPolicy, never the exported mutable array.
- Snapshots must NOT inherit resolveDeliveryPolicy's absent/null -> legacy compatibility: a v2 deliveryPolicy that is missing, null or undefined throws. A v1-labelled object that carries deliveryPolicy is malformed.
- Declaring Task/ExecutionAttempt.executionPolicySnapshot does not make it daemon-owned. WS UPDATE_TASK uses a denylist, so a plugin could already write unknown keys; stripping belongs to CQ-M01c. No code in this task may read the field as authority.
- capture must stay pure: no assertExecutionProfileReady (hand-edited verified-local settings must still capture so later admission can refuse visibly), no state, no writes.
- Do not test or alter evaluateDeliveryEvidence for verified-local snapshots (CQ-M01f changes it). Only lock in that non-strict snapshots neither freeze nor relax the live policy.
- The epic forbids ranking delivery policies with a generic max(); v2 defines no ordering.
- schema.ts is CRLF in this checkout, delivery/*.ts are LF. The shared tree has about 1164 peer/pre-existing dirty paths, including packages/moe-daemon/package-lock.json: touch only the four owned files and report them in modifiedFiles.
- Global forbidden pattern: the dunder-proto property name must not appear anywhere, even in tests. Use Object.create for prototype cases.
